local.body:
Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason’s market, has agreed to a record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday.

The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical.

Skubal’s deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher’s average annual salary was $ 43.33 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.

It’s the fourth largest deal among all baseball players, trailing Juan Soto’s $765 million, Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s $500 million.

Skubal’s agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said.

He joins a Mets team that finished last in the NL East at 74-88 despite having baseball’s highest payroll on opening day at roughly $352 million. New York’s starters had a 4.47 ERA, ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal will top a rotation featuring youngsters Nolan McLean and Christian Scott, with veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga also under contract.

Skubal had plans to meet with at least six teams this month, including the Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres. His deal comes about a week before MLB owners are expected to lock out the players in a labor fight centering on management’s push for a salary cap. MLB has proposed a hard cap of $258.2 million for 2028. Skubal and Soto alone would account for nearly 40% of that cap.

A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings.

Dylan Rourke, who voices Jason, had a brief but memorable appearance on the long-running sitcom.

Rourke's "Modern Family" moment comes midway through Season 8 in an episode titled "Snow Ball." The episode revolves around Manny (Rico Rodriguez) and Luke (Nolan Gould) attempting to put on the school's winter dance and, as always, hilarity ensues. Rourke plays one of the students attending the dance, credited as "Big Guy," and appears in two scenes. In the first, he's picked on by a school bully, and in the second, he interrupts Manny's big speech by asking, "Who are you?"

It was a small appearance, but a far cry from Rourke's considerably larger role as Jason in "Grand Theft Auto VI."

ABC Humor has long been part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise, and Dylan Rourke has plenty of comedic experience himself. He has a background in sketch comedy, having trained with The Groundlings, Second City, and Upright Citizens Brigade. He even appeared on stage with legendary comedian Fred Willard in Willard's sketch comedy show.

When it comes to television, his résumé includes multiple appearances in popular shows aside from "Modern Family." He's made several appearances in the Shonda-verse, including three episodes of "Station 19" and one episode of "Grey's Anatomy," which is considered one of the best ABC shows of all time . His longest-running television role to date was a seven-episode stint on "In the Vault," a murder mystery series where he appeared alongside Sydney Sweeney.

Since his casting in "Grand Theft Auto VI" was revealed, Rourke has said little publicly about the experience. However, on the day of the game's release, he shared a joint Instagram statement with Manni L. Perez, who voices the female protagonist, Lucia . "We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower," the pair wrote. The role marks Rourke's biggest project to date.

entertainment.body:
Dating is all about kissing a frog or two—and possibly a roach?

As the culture of dating continues to swipe its way forward, new terminology also crawls onto the scene, and the language doesn’t always create a beautiful mental image.

Take, for example, “roaching,” which refers to when one person is dating multiple people at once without telling the other individuals that they’re also talking to others.

"The name comes from the saying that if you see one cockroach, there are many more hiding,” dating coach Amy Chan told USA Today in an interview published Nov. 23. “In terms of dating, when you find out there’s one other person, that tends to mean there are several more."

And as the author of Unsingle: How to Date Smarter and Create Love That Lasts author explained, "This often happens in the early stages of dating, where commitment and labels aren’t clearly defined, so they justify that they’re not doing anything wrong."

The consciousness of someone’s actions also plays a part in roaching, like with “intentional roaching.”

"They intentionally conceal the fact that there are other people in the picture," Chan continued. "They’re lying by omitting information."

But when the truth comes out, the roach might not be able to survive the apocalyptic impact their actions had on the other person.

“New York City has shaped the sound of music for generations,” Espinal said in a statement. “But being a great city for music should also mean being a great city for the people who make it. That’s why building our music portfolio is a priority for me. Rachael Pazdan brings the experience and relationships to help us get it right. Together, we’ll listen to the industry and work toward making live performances easier, expanding opportunities across all five boroughs, and connecting young New Yorkers to careers in music. Our goal is simple: make New York City the best place in the world to create music, perform music, and make a living in music.”

Pazdan will build on the city’s New York Music Month and its newly launched Music Production Bootcamp, as well as Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s commitment to increase access to entertainment experiences for NYC residents.

Since launching in 2017, New York Music Month has grown to host 38 talks, 21 performances, a conference and a free rehearsal series that offers more than 2,000 hours of free rehearsal space across the city in four locations.

Parzdan has worked with indie music promoter AdHoc, helping the company become a full-service creative agency that served clients including Bryant Park, Pitchfork, A2IM and BandLab. While at the company, she also helped promote events including Global Citizen in New York City and Johannesburg.

She also served as a booker for numerous independent venues across New York City, including Public Records, The Bell House and Le Poisson Rouge, and produced the short-form docuseries Stories from the Stage, which shared stories from New York City’s independent venues and promoters during the pandemic.

entertainment.title: Even Sienna Miller Was Surprised by That ‘War’ Ending
entertainment.summary: The female lead of the HBO/Sky legal drama's first season, who is no stranger to weathering tabloid scrutiny herself, opens up to THR about who came out on top in the high-profile divorce in the end.
entertainment.body:
Logo text [This story contains MAJOR spoilers from the War finale.]

Sienna Miller doesn’t quite know why she keeps getting tapped to play women caught up in the public eye. Since breaking out two decades ago as Edie Sedgwick in Factory Girl , the American-born English actress has made a speciality out of portraying women navigating intense media scrutiny — from Alfred Hitchcock’s tormented muse Tippi Hedren in The Girl to the embattled political wives of Showtime’s The Loudest Voice and Netflix’s Anatomy of a Scandal .

“I think it’s less that I’m seeking out these roles and more that those are the roles that people see me as, probably because a famous actress is part of my identity in a way [but] I don’t feel is part of me,” Miller tells The Hollywood Reporter on a recent video call from her home in the U.K. “I feel like an actor who’s not very famous — and a mom. But it’s quite funny to perhaps send myself up by playing heightened versions of whatever I imagine people might assume that to be.” Related Stories TV All's Fair in Love and 'War': Creator George Kay Explains His Ruling on Morgan and Carla's Divorce TV Archie Renaux on 'War's Resident -- and Misunderstood -- Bad Boy

Miller’s latest TV role is no exception. In creator George Kay’s HBO/Sky legal anthology drama War , which just aired its finale on Thursday in the U.S., Miller plays film star Clara Duval, whose messy, high-profile divorce from Dominic West’s billionaire tech founder Morgan Henderson becomes a feeding frenzy for both the press and their ruthless legal teams. At the center of the dispute is an equitable split of Zephyr — the ostensibly “less toxic” social media platform that Morgan built after watching Carla endure relentless online bullying and that Carla named after Mary Darby Robinson’s poem “Ode to the Muse.”

Though their lawyers push them toward scorched-earth tactics to win at all costs, the pair ultimately choose to settle on their own terms, resulting in a surprisingly optimistic portrait of life after separation. “I think the normalizing of divorce is something that should be more commonplace in the world. It doesn’t have to be hell,” Miller says. “I thought that the ending was very poignant and sweet.”

In the wide-ranging chat below, Miller opens up to THR about shedding her own people-pleasing tendencies to play a “narcissistic” (but surprisingly sympathetic) actress, why she thinks Carla really came out on top in the divorce — and how she reflects now on her own experience of being tabloid fodder in her 20s: “I’m more in a kind of anthropological way interested in it [now], because I feel maybe from some PTSD that I am separate from it.”

entertainment.title: Two-time Oscar winner claims he’s struggling to find work: ‘No roles for me’
entertainment.summary: "There’s more good actors than there is good material,” the "Moonlight" star recently said on Carmelo Anthony's “7PM in Brooklyn” podcast.
entertainment.body:
Mahershala Ali revealed he is struggling to find work — despite already winning two Oscars.

“There’s more good actors than there is good material,” the “Moonlight” star recently said on Carmelo Anthony’s “7PM in Brooklyn” podcast.

“It’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots,” he added.

“It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes.”

Ali, 52, said that in the “vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those.”

“You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars,” he explained.

“If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.”

Though Ali noted that actors can take matters into their own hands and produce their own projects, he said that can take anywhere from three to five years.

entertainment.title: Mary J. Blige ‘Real Love’ Lawsuit Rejected by Appeals Court: ‘Notably Different’
entertainment.summary: The ruling dismissed a case that claimed Blige's decades-old hit illegally borrowed from a 1973 funk song with a rich history of hip-hop sampling.
entertainment.body:
A lawsuit over Mary J. Blige ’s 1992 hit “Real Love” has been rejected by a federal appeals court, ending a long-running case that claimed it featured a legendary 1973 funk sample without a license.

Filed in 2024 against Universal Music Group (UMG) by Tuff City Records, the lawsuit alleged Blige’s track illegally borrowed from “Impeach the President” by the Honey Drippers — an oft-sampled piece of hip-hop history that’s been used by Run-DMC , Dr. Dre and Doja Cat .

“While ‘Impeach the President’ and ‘Real Love’ share certain percussive elements, other elements are notably different,” the appeals court wrote. “Music borrows, and must necessarily borrow, and use[s] much which was well known and used before.”

The ruling upheld an earlier decision by a lower judge that had dismissed Tuff City’s case last year, and echoed that judge’s conclusion: that the overall songs are so different that an ordinary listener would be unlikely to even recognize the earlier song.

“The songs’ total concept and overall feel reinforce the conclusion that the works at issue are not substantially similar,” the appeals court wrote in Monday’s decision. “Applying our good ears and common sense, we conclude that the works as a whole are distinct. The songs differ in their lyrics, melody, genre, subject matter, and overall sound.”

“Real Love” spent 31 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1992, reaching a peak of No. 7 on the chart. It has remained one of Blige’s most enduring hits, with more than 137 million streams on Spotify and a movie adaptation released by Lifetime in 2023.

Like many other hip-hop tracks, “Real Love” featured elements of “Impeach the President,” a 1973 protest funk song that later became a popular sample in the early days of rap. It seemingly ended up in Blige’s song indirectly, via a direct sample of the 1987 hip-hop track “Top Billin’” by the Brooklyn duo Audio Two, who had themselves sampled the Honey Drippers’ song.

Decades after “Real Love” was released, Tuff City sued UMG over the alleged sample in April 2024, claiming the company was aware of the problem but had done nothing about it. And during the litigation, UMG effectively conceded that Blige’s song had indeed copied material from “Impeach.”

entertainment.title: Danny Boyle on ‘Ink’ and Murdoch, the ‘Trainspotting’ Toilet Scene and How ‘Slumdog Millionaire’ Almost Went Straight to Video
entertainment.summary: The Oscar-winning filmmaker spoke with The Hollywood Reporter in front of an audience at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival, where he was honored with the Maverick Director Award.
entertainment.body:
“Decades before clickbait, before Fox News, before OnlyFans, before Truth Social, before Google, before Facebook, before any of it , something started that we’re still living with the consequences of,” Danny Boyle said while recording an episode of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast in front of an audience at the recent SCAD Savannah Film Festival , where he was being honored with the fest’s Maverick Director Award. The Oscar-winning director was referring to the fateful 1969 meeting of Australian businessman Rupert Murdoch and British newspaperman Larry Lamb, and the tabloid journalism that it spawned, which is chronicled in Boyle’s latest film, Ink , which Netflix will release in theaters on Dec. 11 and on its streaming platform on Jan. 8. Related Stories SCAD Savannah Film Festival 'American Doctor' Director on Her Powerful Gaza Doc: "I Wanted to Do Something" Movies Ron Howard Wasn't Sure He Was the Right Director for 'Avedon'; This Is What Changed His Mind

The 70-year-old Englishman has directed 15 features over the past 32 years, including 1994’s Shallow Grave , 1996’s Trainspotting , 2002’s 28 Days Later , 2008’s Slumdog Millionaire , 2010’s 127 Hours and 2015’s Steve Jobs . Described by the New York Times as “a cinematic hypnotist” and by The Guardian as “a film director in a class of his own,” he won best director Academy, Golden Globe and BAFTA awards for Slumdog , and an Emmy for his work on the London 2012 Olympic Games Opening Ceremony. And he also was presented with a Britannia Award for Artistic Excellence in 2009 and a BFI Fellowship in 2010.

You can watch the listen to or watch the entire episode above, or read select excerpts below…

On the scene in Trainspotting in which Ewan McGregor swims through “the worst toilet in Scotland”…

“CG was just beginning to emerge in cinemas. In fact, there was a Christmas film out at the time with Tim Allen playing Santa Clause, and they squeezed him into a chimney pot. That’s one of the very first uses of CG in film. It looked terrible, I thought. I thought, ‘We’re not going to do it like that,’ because somebody said, ‘Oh, you could use CG,’ as it was at the time. We wanted to do it live. So we used a theater trick, the trompe l’oeil: you cut the toilet in half and film it from the side. So, obviously, it isn’t a toilet on this side; it’s the slide that McGregor goes down. Then Brian [Tufano, the cinematographer] told Ewan [McGregor, the film’s star] to twist his feet ’round at the end, because then people will think it’s the U-bend that you’re going ’round, which curiously people do. It’s just that illusion that we buy into. If you believe the actors, you’ll believe anything! So people believed it was the worst toilet in Scotland, even though it smelled of chocolate, because all the shit was chocolate, and it was delicious! All the prop girls had candles burning so that everybody felt good about being there all day.”

entertainment.title: 5 Classic TV Shows That Paved The Way For Reacher
entertainment.summary: Reacher has been breaking records left and right, but Lee Child's TV adaptation stands on the shoulders of several other classic TV shows that share its themes.
entertainment.body:
Amazon Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Reacher" is one of Amazon Prime's most successful series. Featuring Alan Ritchson as the nomadic ex-Army investigator Jack Reacher, the third season garnered 54.6 million views within 19 days of its release. The action-packed adaptation of Lee Child's book series was already renewed for a sixth season ahead of its fifth. Viewers love the series' continuous action, and readers of the book appreciate its faithfulness to the source material. Ritchson's performance as the muscular drifter with no belongings is also frequently lauded.

However, "Reacher" is not the first series to feature a lone hero using his strength, training, and intelligence to fight injustice and help others. Throughout television history, there have been a number of action series that have used these core elements. The older generation of action fans were certainly spoiled, so to pay respect to the television action heroes that came before, here is a list of five classic shows that built the foundation "Reacher" stands on.

CBS This CBS series ran for four seasons and featured Edward Woodward as Robert McCall, a former government spy. McCall worked all around New York City administering vigilante justice and protecting anyone who contacted him through a classified ad he put out in the newspaper.

In contrast to the mostly rural areas that Jack Reacher visits, "The Equalizer" utilizes the gritty, metropolitan atmosphere of New York City. However, just like Reacher, McCall has a highly trained background that heavily emphasizes investigation and recon. Both he and Jack Reacher use this to their advantage when they have to track someone down or fight an enemy. "The Equalizer" also saw McCall using impressive fighting skills, even if not possessing the muscular frame Ritchson does on his own show. And while he mostly operated independently, he still received help from dedicated allies he's worked with in the past. Jack Reacher receives similar help in the show, primarily from Frances Neagley (Maria Sten).

CBS Years before playing NYPD commissioner Frank Reagan on "Blue Bloods," Tom Selleck played the titular private investigator on "Magnum, P.I." Like "Reacher," this CBS series had its main character going around and helping solve problems associated with crime and protection. However, the show's famous Hawaiian setting and the lavish estate that Magnum lives on are a stark contrast to Reacher's minimalist, wandering style.

entertainment.title: Rita Wilson Reveals Surprising Truth About Her Massive Back Tattoo
entertainment.summary: Rita Wilson is making her mark. Two months debuting a massive cross on her back, sparking speculation that she had gotten a tattoo to match ink sported by her and Tom Hanks' son Chet Hanks, the...
entertainment.body:
Two months debuting a massive cross on her back , sparking speculation that she had gotten a tattoo to match ink sported by her and Tom Hanks ' son Chet Hanks , the "Stranger With Age" singer clarified if she had actually gotten some body art.

“It was a prank that I did for my son’s birthday, who has a lot of tattoos,” Rita emphasized during a Nov. 23 appearance on CBS Mornings . “I used to threaten him with getting a tattoo, and I would say, ‘You better watch out.'"

And while the temporary body art was "definitely a different look," the 70-year-old explained that she won't be going under the needle for real any time soon.

As Rita—who also shares son Truman Hanks , 30, with Tom and is stepmom to the Oscar winner's kids Colin Hanks , 48, and E.A. Hanks , 40, from his first marriage—put it, “My daughter said, ‘The new tattoo is not having a tattoo.’”

Still, Chet appreciated the sentiment. After all, the 36-year-old and his mom share the same sense of humor.

"He’s a character," Rita raved in an April interview with The Independent . "He’s so eccentric.”

In fact, the Runaway Bride actress believed Chet "is the person I could never have been at that age."

"He’s just out there being himself, take it or leave it," she continued. "I love that."

entertainment.title: Miley Cyrus Celebrates 34th Birthday With Look at Maxx Morando Wedding
entertainment.summary: Miley Cyrus has turned the rest of her life into a holiday. As the Hannah Montana alum turned 34 on Nov. 23, she gave fans a special gift: a peek into her and Maxx Morando’s wedding...
entertainment.body:
As the Hannah Montana alum turned 34 on Nov. 23, she gave fans a special gift: a peek into her and Maxx Morando ’s wedding celebration .

“Waking up on my 34th birthday feeling so grateful,” Cyrus posted to Instagram alongside a carousel of photos from the Nov. 21 ceremony in Palm Springs, Calif . “Thank you for all the wishes & to everyone who made this weekend a memory we’ll cherish for a lifetime and beyond.”

Among the snaps she included a look at something beautiful: her wedding accessories, including her white heels, her and Morando’s wedding rings, as well as sunglasses and a purse.

The “Wrecking Ball” singer— who wore a long-sleeved, backless wedding gown designed by Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello —posted a few snaps from the wedding itself as she and Morando stood under a floral awning at the Frank Sinatra Twin Palms Estate.

The photos also included several of Cyrus with her family, including one grooving with mom Tish Cyrus and sister Noah Cyrus , as well as another loving look at her and dad Billy Ray Cyrus sharing a father-daughter dance.

The Grammy winner also reshared the carousel to her Instagram Stories, set to her song “Let’s Get Married” from her 2026 album Bass Persuasion .

Cyrus—who was previously married to Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2020—began dating Morando in 2021 , with the Liily drummer revealing they crossed paths after the friend of his bandmate’s sister set them up on a blind date. As he told Wonderland magazine in July, they hit it off immediately and “just never stopped hanging out.”

And Cyrus knew exactly what it was about an angel like Morando , to whom she got engaged in 2025, that made their romance work.

On Nov. 7, comedian and online/social media creator Druski will make his hosting debut (his booking was first reported at Puck ). entertainment.title: Inside the ‘Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic’: A Recipe for Blending Brands With TV (and a Full-Circle Career Moment for Host Drew Barrymore)
entertainment.summary: The special airs Monday night on CBS.
entertainment.body:
The folks behind CBS ‘ Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic are hoping to make this holiday special an annual Thanksgiving week tradition.

“I feel like this is going to become part of our cultural tradition,” says Scott Weintrob, founder of Studio Large Eyes and executive producer of the special. “Every Thanksgiving for the next 10 years, with the Pillsbury Bake-Off as the trigger to Thanksgiving week.”

The show is actually a collaboration between CBS and General Mills — which, incidentally, owns the “Bake-Off” trademark in the United States. (“Which is why they cannot call The Great British Bake Off the Bake Off in the U.S. and they have to call it The Great British Baking Show, ” says Lisa Balzo, head of brand studio partnerships at General Mills .) Related Stories TV 'Survivor 51' Star Lewis Kelly on His $1 Million Coin Flip and Joining the Cast at the Last Minute TV CBS Inks New Deal to Air Kennedy Center Honors

Balzo notes that GM, parent company of Pillsbury, had been interested in the idea of a “big grand spectacle” that would incorporate one of the company’s brands. She had already met Weintrob previously at an industry event, and the two began having conversations about some options. “I started talking [with Weintrob] about the history of the Bake-Off, and how it used to be this kind of big grand spectacle that was put on as a live event,” she says. “Over the years, we’ve done various different things with it, and it’s become a smaller digital activation. We’ve also collaborated with the Food Network. I mentioned to Scott that we have been talking about, for years, wanting to bring it back to its full glory. And he pitched this incredible live event.”

“What I originally said to them was, I love the format of the Westminster Dog Show as a baking show, a large event as a live, two-hour special focusing on ordinary people doing extraordinary things,” Weintrob recalls. They agreed on the idea and decided that Thanksgiving would be a key time for the project to air. “I felt we had the opportunity to go and talk to distributors about making this wonderful event. And that’s the key word: It’s an event.”

Balzo says the concept “felt so perfect” and “felt very serendipitous to me at the time. He had this project in his head that that was so perfectly aligned with Pillsbury and what we were looking to do with the Bake Off.”

Back to that trademark: Pillsbury held its first Bake-Off in 1949, when it was called Pillsbury’s Best Grand National Baking Contest. A total of 100 finalists went to New York to compete, and each received at least $100 and kept the G.E. stove they baked on. Eleanor Roosevelt presented the grand prizes, which ranged from $25,000 to $50,000.

entertainment.title: Poker Face Reboot Starring Peter Dinklage Not Moving Forward, Rian Johnson Says

entertainment.body:
Monica Schipper/WireImage Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Sorry, "Poker Face" fans, but we won't get to see Peter Dinklage take the reins from Natasha Lyonne after all.

A proposed third season of the canceled mystery-comedy, with Dinklage taking over for Lyonne as Charlie Cale, is not moving forward, co-creator Rian Johnson revealed in a Variety interview. "At the moment it's in its resting place," Johnson admitted. "I got very excited about the notion of going out there with Dinklage, but then the more we kind of explored it, the more it kind of didn't really make sense." He added, though, that "hopefully I can do something else with him someday. He's the best."

Johnson first floated the idea of Dinklage taking over the Charlie Cale role when "Poker Face" was canceled at Peacock last November after two seasons, with a plan to shop the rebooted series to other networks. "We've been germinating this next move together since writing the Season 2 finale," Johnson and Lyonne said in a joint statement. "We love our 'Poker Face' and this is the perfect way to keep it rolling. Give us a beat and we may just see Charlie Cale again down that open highway."

Peacock "Poker Face" debuted on Peacock in 2023, with Natasha Lyonne starring as Charlie Cale, a Vegas cocktail waitress who had the strange ability to tell if someone is lying. Each episode saw Charlie traveling to a new town and meeting a fresh set of characters while investigating a murder. ( Read our initial review here .) Lyonne earned an Emmy nomination for the first season, and the show returned last year for a 12-episode sophomore run. ( Check out our finale recap .)

Dinklage — best known for playing Tyrion Lannister on HBO's "Game of Thrones," a role that won him four Emmys for best supporting actor in a drama — has been busy on the small screen as of late. He joined Michael C. Hall on the Showtime revival "Dexter: Resurrection" and co-starred with Ethan Hawke on FX's "The Lowdown," and he'll next be seen in Season 2 of the FX sci-fi drama "Alien: Earth."

entertainment.summary: Mary Star of the Sea will also return to streaming services, where it hasn't been available for years
entertainment.body:
Zwan , the short-lived supergroup led by Smashing Pumpkins ’ Billy Corgan and Jimmy Chamberlin , will reissue their first and only album, Mary Star of the Sea , with a bunch of new archival material .

The reissue will feature a newly mixed version of Mary Star of the Sea , overseen by Corgan and engineer Nikola Dokic. It’ll also boast 19 previously unreleased demos and outtakes, released under the name Rooms Full of Salt . The reissue will be available as a special four-LP vinyl set on standard black vinyl and a limited edition “Ocean Illusionist” color variant. And it’ll bring Mary Star of the Sea to streaming services, where it’s been unavailable for years.

To tease the project, Zwan released two songs, “Declarations of Faith,” a track off the original album, and one of the unreleased tracks, “The Empty Sea.”

Vinyl pre-orders for the Mary Star of the Sea will begin this Friday, Nov. 27, with orders expected to ship out in December. ( Mary Star of the Sea will hit streaming services after the vinyl editions are released, Corgan’s reps said, though an exact date wasn’t given.)

Corgan and Chamberlin formed Zwan in 2001 after the Smashing Pumpkins split. They filled out their ranks with three other Nineties alt rock vets, guitarists Matt Sweeney (Chavez, Skunk) and David Pajo (Slint), and bassist Paz Lenchantin (A Perfect Circle). Mary Star of the Sea was released in January 2003 and reached Number Three on the Billboard 200 Albums chart. Lead single, “Honestly,” also became a Top 10 hit on rock and alternative radio. Zwan disbanded in 2003.

entertainment.title: ‘East of Eden’ Star Hoon Lee on the “Honor” of Playing Lee and Why It Made Sense to Expand on the Character
entertainment.summary: The actor also commends the show's creator Zoe Kazan and her dedication to story: "I don't think anyone in the world knows this text better than Zoe."
entertainment.body:
“It’s a huge relief,” says Hoon Lee of the reaction to East of Eden . “With any production, people work very hard. But I think this one in particular, there was the weight of expectation and wanting to honor the source material that adds a slightly different dimension.”

The actor stars as Lee in Zoe Kazan’s adaptation of the classic John Steinbeck novel, released last month. The Florence Pugh-fronted series was quickly met with praise. “It almost would’ve been worse if it came out with a sort of indifference, like met with a wave of shrugging,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter . “To be well received the way the project has is obviously the best possible outcome and it’s very, very gratifying.” Related Stories Critics' Conversation The Best Fall TV Shows Hurt So Good TV Florence Pugh Was "So Nervous" to Release 'East of Eden' and Still Hasn't Read the Reviews: "It Was Too Much With This One"

The series is very much aligned with the novel, but one of the most significant changes came in the form of the expansion of Lee’s character. He’d been given a head’s up, but he wasn’t sure just how in-depth the story would go until he received the scripts. All he knew was that Kazan and writer Alexander Chee had written a standalone episode for the character, the footage for which ended up being woven into other episodes.

The actor was delighted to see what Kazan had to add and challenges anyone that questions just what the writer knows about the material. “That’s a huge risk for Zoe and the production but that actually speaks a lot to the boldness of her interpretation. There’s a lot of courage there, not only to put that forth, but to do it for the right reasons,” he says.

“I don’t think anyone in the world knows this text better than Zoe. Every move she’s made, there is a reason for it, and there’s a justification in the text,” he continues. “She’s not somebody that is wildly going off script and going off the range to do what she’s doing. It’s a 600- to 800-page book. The idea that any of us who have just read it have all of the detail at our fingertips … But Zoe kind of does. She’s gone to that level.”

The series, much like the novel, is quite heavy. It’s clear from moment one that show isn’t holding any punches. It might not be the easiest to watch in one go. “There should be a dosage that’s recommended,” he says somewhat cheekily. “It is intense.”

entertainment.title: ENHYPEN, Beyond the Vampire Story
entertainment.summary: With THE SIN : PARALLEL WORLD , JUNGWON, JAY, JAKE, SUNGHOON, SUNOO & NI-KI step outside their supernatural universe to explore a more human side.
entertainment.body:
For nearly six years, ENHYPEN have built a musical universe where love, fate and identity are intertwined with the supernatural. Vampires have long been central to that story, allowing the group to explore emotions that transcend the boundaries of ordinary life. But for their latest chapter, ENHYPEN are asking a different question.

That question lies at the heart of THE SIN : PARALLEL WORLD , the group’s new release, officially designated a Spin Off Single . Set in a parallel universe where the characters live as ordinary humans, the project imagines a world free from the rules and restrictions of their vampire existence. Their supernatural lives survive only in dreams, yet their connection remains unchanged: no matter the universe, they are destined to find each other.

For ENHYPEN, the shift is less about leaving their mythology behind than finding a new way to connect it to real life. As JAY explains, exploring the characters as ordinary people allowed the group to approach familiar themes of love and connection from a more relatable perspective.

Across its three tracks, the release explores that idea through distinct musical styles. Lead single “I Want You” pairs warm synthesizers and a four-on-the-floor rhythm with melodies inspired by 2000s pop R&B. “Don’t Stop” takes a sleeker approach, blending minimal trap production with electro-pop and alternative R&B influences. Closing track “ILY Season” turns the group’s attention directly toward ENGENEs, with all six members contributing lyrics and singing the words they wrote.

Speaking with Billboard Korea, ENHYPEN reflect on the creative choices behind THE SIN : PARALLEL WORLD , their growing individual artistic identities and the experiences that continue to shape them both onstage and beyond.

THE SIN: PARALLEL WORLD takes ENHYPEN’s vampire narrative into a parallel universe where the characters live as ordinary humans. Did exploring this more human side of the story give you new creative possibilities, particularly in the emotions or musical styles you wanted to express?

JAY: For the past six years, we’ve been gradually developing our story through this vampire narrative. But we had different goals we wanted to explore with this album, so we decided to use the idea of a parallel universe to deliver our message to ENGENEs in a more direct and realistic way. We wanted to imagine what our relationships would have been like if we were human, and how we might have lived.

entertainment.title: Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie ‘Malibu’ From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: Room 101 also produces director Tod "Kip" Williams' feature about a dog-sitting gig gone wrong.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Sadie Sandler is set to make a splash as she prepares to star in her first horror movie.

The actress, who recently led the Netflix comedy Roommates , will collaborate again with the streamer on the horror feature Malibu , The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Tod “Kip” Williams, known for helming Paranormal Activity 2 , is set to direct the film from a script he wrote with Tom Pabst, who worked on the superhero series Titans .

Production will begin in early 2027 for the feature that counts Roy Lee ‘s Vertigo Entertainment , Steven Schneider’s Room 101 and Adam Sandler ‘s Happy Madison as producers.

Malibu centers on Sadie Sandler as an aspiring actress who accepts a last-minute dog-sitting job at a reclusive movie star’s Malibu mansion. Soon, she learns that the house is not what she expected.

While Sandler appeared in Netflix’s 2020 spooky comedy Hubie Halloween opposite dad Adam Sandler and has voiced a role in Sony Pictures’ animated Hotel Transylvania franchise, Malibu is described as straight horror and is said to carry a much different tone from her previous projects.

Sadie Sandler recently appeared on Netflix’s Nobody Wants This , and her feature credits include Roommates , Jay Kelly , Happy Gilmore 2 and You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah .

In addition to helming Paranormal Activity 2 , Williams directed John Cusack and Samuel L. Jackson in the 2016 movie Cell that adapted Stephen King’s sci-fi horror novel.

Lee, who was named THR’ s producer of the year in 2025, has served as executive producer on such horror series as Peacock’s Crystal Lake and HBO’s It: Welcome to Derry . His recent feature credits include Resident Evil , Weapons , A Minecraft Movie and Obsession director Curry Barker’s forthcoming movie Anything but Ghosts .

entertainment.summary: Wham!’s “Last Christmas” and Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” go on their latest chart sleigh rides.
entertainment.body:
Karol G , Judeline and rusowsky’s “BbY WOW” rebounds a spot for a spot for a seventh week at No. 1 on the Billboard Global 200 . Meanwhile, the song continues for an eighth week atop Billboard Global Excl. U.S.

“BbY WOW” drew 36.5 million streams globally Nov. 13-19, according to Luminate. The song, which first topped both charts in mid-September, totaled 29.8 million streams outside the U.S. in the tracking week.

Ashe’s “Stop the Wedding!” rises 3-2 for a new Global 200 high and Tate McRae’s “Housewife” slides two spots to No. 3 after reigning in its first four weeks.

Wham!’s “Last Christmas” (8-4) and Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” (14-5) decorate the Global 200’s top five, with 28.8 million and 26 million streams, respectively, worldwide. Wham!’s 1984 classic reached No. 1 on the chart, for two weeks, for the first time last year, while Carey’s, from 1994, upped its count to 20 weeks on top — the most since the list began in 2020.

“Stop the Wedding!” likewise lifts 3-2 for a new Global Excl. U.S. best; “Housewife” drops 2-3, after it led for three weeks; and Jamie Miller’s “Babydoll” bumps 5-4 for a new high.

“Last Christmas” surges 17-5 on Global Excl. U.S. (18.5 million streams outside the U.S.) and “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” 35-8 (16 million). As on the Global 200, the former spent its first two weeks at No. 1 on Global Excl. U.S. last holiday season; the latter has led for 14 weeks.

The Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. U.S. charts rank songs based on streaming and sales activity culled from more than 200 territories around the world, as compiled by Luminate. The Global 200 is inclusive of worldwide data and the Global Excl. U.S. chart comprises data from territories excluding the United States.

Chart ranks are based on a weighted formula incorporating official-only streams on both subscription and ad-supported tiers of audio and video music services, as well as download sales, the latter of which reflect purchases from full-service digital music retailers from around the world, with sales from direct-to-consumer (D2C) sites excluded from the charts’ calculations.

entertainment.title: D’Angelo’s Estate Releases Posthumous Song ‘Kamikazi’ for ‘GTA 6’: Singer ‘Approved This Track’ Before His Death
entertainment.summary: "He was enthusiastic ... to have this record included in the game," his brother said in a statement.
entertainment.body:
D’Angelo ‘s estate has confirmed the late singer has a song in Grand Theft Auto VI .

As gamers made their way through GTA 6 after its release Nov. 19, news broke that there might be an unreleased song by the musician born Michael Archer that plays on one of the many radio stations that Rockstar Games has curated for its latest iteration of Vice City. This was later confirmed when Rockstar dropped the credits of everyone involved with “Kamikazi” being listed under Worldwide FM’s “Songs” list. So while driving around Leonida, turn to Worldwide FM hosted by Giles Peterson on the radio dial, and players will be able to listen to an unreleased D’Angelo song as they’re on the way to hit their next lick.

Rockstar and the late singer’s relationship go back a ways because of D’Angelo’s love for Red Dead Redemption . He loved that game so much, he reached out to the video-game developer and was allowed to be a play tester for Red Dead Redemption 2 before it’s 2018 release, which led to him crafting the original song “May I? Stand Unshaken” for the game’s soundtrack.

“He would come in here [Rockstar’s New York city office] and just play the game. We weren’t even talking about doing music,” Ivan Pavlovich, director of music and audio at Rockstar Games, told Rolling Stone in 2018. “When D’Angelo comes through, he shows up at midnight, and he’s playing the game until four in the morning. Each time he was just like, ‘It’s incredible.’ It just blows his mind. He’s such a fan. I have never seen someone that excited.”

The singer’s brother Luther Archer, Jr. released a lengthy statement on behalf of the Estate of Michael D’Angelo Archer about the official release of “Kamikazi”:

It is still hard for so many of us to accept, but it has been a little over a year since we lost my brother Michael, who you know as D’Angelo. When it came to his art he was infinitely principled — he was an unshakeable force of artistic integrity and supreme aptitude. He was a singular genius and we are profoundly blessed to have shared our time with him — his undeniable gift from God was powerful beyond any words I can find.

I have been given from Michael an incredibly daunting task in overseeing the release of his posthumous works. It is a mission that must be taken on with the exacting standards and integrity that our beloved would’ve insisted upon. Fully without compromise. To that end we, the Estate of Michael D’Angelo Archer, in pursuit of the infinite impact of his life’s work and in accordance with his wishes, are proud to announce the release of his song … Michael approved this track in its current form in November of 2024 to be released as part of Grand Theft Auto VI . He was a tremendous admirer of Rockstar Games and a past collaborator of theirs, and he was enthusiastic (to say the least) to have this record included in the game and released to a wide audience as a single. “Kamikazi” was produced by D’Angelo himself, alongside Slingbaum and engineer/trusted ally Ben Kane.

sports.title: Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs listed as limited in practice again on Monday
sports.summary: The Packers' injury report for Monday looks a lot like the one they turned in on Sunday.
sports.body:
Defensive end Micah Parsons (knee) and running back Josh Jacobs (finger) remained limited participants. Parsons is expected to make his 2026 debut on Wednesday night against the Rams and Jacobs is trying to return after missing the Packers’ last game in Week 10.

Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), offensive lineman Travis Glover (shoulder), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), wide receiver Bo Melton (thigh), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) were limited participants. Glover was the only new addition to that group on Monday.

Cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib) moved from limited to full participation while guard Aaron Banks (knee) remained in that category.

sports.title: Rams upgrade RB Kyren Williams to full participant on Monday's injury report
sports.summary: While any injury news about the Rams has largely been bad this season, there was a positive development on the team's Monday practice report.
sports.body:
Running back Kyren Williams (toe) was upgraded from a limited to a full participant in the day’s session.

Williams With how many skill players are unavailable, Williams presence is critical for both the run and pass game. He leads the team with 616 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns. He also has 38 catches for 267 yards with a TD in 2026.

Safety Kam Curl (toe) was also upgraded from a non-participant on Sunday to limited on Monday.

Offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), offensive lineman Coleman Shelton (hamstring), and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not participate, with Ferguson set to stay on injured reserve for the rest of the season as he undergoes ankle surgery.

Defensive end Aaron Donald, outside linebacker Myles Garrett, tight end Tyler Higbee, and outside linebacker Byron Young all received a rest day.

Tight end Davis Allen (oblique), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), offensive lineman Justin Dedich (hand), linebacker Nate Landman (toe), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), defensive end Kobie Turner (groin), and quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) were al full participants.

sports.title: Marlon Humphrey back with Ravens, Jesse Minter doesn't commit to Week 12 return to lineup
sports.summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was back at the team's facility on Monday.
sports.body:
The Ravens sent Humphrey home last week and deactivated him for Sunday’s loss to the Panthers after Humphrey made derogatory comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Humphrey apologized, but Minter said the decision to sit him out last week was made after conversations inside the organization.

Minter did not divulge details of that conversation and declined to share any of what he and Humphrey talked about on Monday. He said a decision on Humphrey’s return against the Texans in Week 12 will be made later in the week.

“I expect us to work through the week and see where we’re at,” Minter said.

Humphrey started the first 10 games of the season and has 40 tackles, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery this year.

sports.title: Bengals activate LB Swayze Bozeman, G Brian Parker from injured reserve
sports.summary: The Bengals announced a pair of roster moves on Monday afternoon.
sports.body:
Linebacker Swayze Bozeman and guard Brian Parker have both been activated from injured reserve. They will both be available to play against the Commanders in Monday night’s game in Washington.

Bozeman was claimed off of waivers during the offseason and he appeared in four games before going on injured reserve with a forearm injury. He had four tackles while playing a regular role on special teams in those contests.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and he was placed on injured reserve at the end of August. Parker has been dealing with a knee injury.

sports.title: DK Metcalf will not be suspended for actions during Steelers-Eagles
sports.summary: According to multiple reports, while Metcalf has avoided a suspension, he may still be fined.
sports.body:
Metcalf was ejected for committing two unsportsmanlike conduct fouls over the course of the game.

Metcalf then left the locker room without speaking to reporters. But spoke to them on Monday, denying the accusation that he was trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

It’s been a trying year for Metcalf, who has just 36 catches for 434 yards with two touchdowns in 10 games. That the receiver will not be suspended is a positive development for him. But Pittsburgh would surely like to see Metcalf increase his production and reduce the on-field antics that do not help the team.

sports.title: Commanders activate Jacory Croskey-Merritt
sports.summary: The Commanders have made an addition to their offensive backfield ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.
sports.body:
Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was activated from injured reserve on Monday afternoon. The Commanders released cornerback Isaac Yiadom in a corresponding move.

Croskey-Merritt was a full participant in practice this week and he was listed as questionable on Washington’s final injury report. He has missed the last four games with a groin injury.

Croskey-Merritt had 67 carries for 239 yards and two touchdowns in five games before his injury.

The Commanders listed Rachaad White as questionable with a heel injury that kept him out of practice Saturday. Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry are the other backs on the active roster for Washington.

sports.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
sports.summary: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.
sports.body:
Head coach John Harbaugh said at his Monday press conference that Newsome suffered a high-ankle sprain. Harbaugh said that Newsome will be out multiple weeks as a result of the injury.

Newsome only played four snaps before being forced out of Sunday’s game. He has 35 tackles, an interception and eight passes defensed in his nine appearances this season.

That play earned Newsome a three-year extension beyond the one-year deal he signed with the team in the offseason, but the Giants will have to turn elsewhere in the secondary for the near future.

sports.title: Vikings "don't necessarily expect" Jordan Addison back this week
sports.summary: The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.
sports.body:
Addison has missed the last two games with a thumb injury that required surgery, but O’Connell said last week that the outlook was “really encouraging” for Addison’s return. The Vikings opted not to put him on injured reserve, which points to a return before missing four games but O’Connell didn’t make it sound like that would happen against the Falcons this week.

“Encouraged a bout where Jordan’s at,” O’Connell said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. “Don’t necessarily expect to have him this week but he’s progressing really well for having just gotten that thing fixed.”

The Vikings will host the Panthers in Week 13 and O’Connell’s next update on Addison’s progress may not come until closer to that matchup.

sports.title: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis
sports.summary: Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator.
sports.body:
The Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

Rallis, 33, was retained under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur after previously serving in the same role under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Rallis came with Gannon from Philadelphia, where Gannon had served as defensive coordinator and Rallis was linebackers coach.

The Cardinals have struggled mightily on defense this season, with the unit currently ranked No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 31 in points allowed. The team had offered little resistance in losses to the Rams and Chiefs in consecutive weeks, with both teams scoring 34 points.

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator. He was Pittsburgh’s DC under Mike Tomlin from 2022 to 2025. He previously served as defensive coordinator for the Lions and Bengals.

sports.title: Super Bowl LXI will be shown in IMAX theaters
sports.summary: The Super Bowl will be shown on some very big screens this season.
sports.body:
ESPN’s broadcast of Super Bowl LXI will be shown live in IMAX theaters as part of an agreement among the NFL, Disney and IMAX.

The game will air live in IMAX theaters in the U.S., Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. The show will include the game itself, the halftime show, pregame and postgame.

IMAX has grown increasingly popular for its huge, curved screens and immersive sound. The format is known for movies like The Odyssey , not for live sports, but the opportunity to watch the Super Bowl on the biggest screen in town will draw plenty of fans who will be curious to see what the game looks like on a screen so big that the players are larger than life.

sports.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
sports.summary: One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.
sports.body:
Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

Ferguson was on track to return earlier this month before suffering a hamstring injury at practice.

But now his ankle has not responded to treatment the way he or the team anticipated.

“ Didn’t necessarily feel great , but he had a really good week of practice but you could still see he was kind of getting comfortable,” McVay said of the process with Ferguson, via Adam Grosbard of the Southern California News Group. “Took some meds to be able to do that. Gets the hamstring on a Friday, and then, as he’s really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it, and it was like something in his deltoid and his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want.

“I don’t know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it’s just not coming along, and he wouldn’t be able to be himself and put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete, some of the change of direction, moving him across the formation.”

Ferguson is now set to remain on injured reserve for the rest of the year.

A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Ferguson was able to appear in just three games this year, catching seven passes for 63 yards with a touchdown. He caught 11 passes for 231 yards with three TDs in 14 games as a rookie last year.

sports.title: Shane Steichen says Colts have not shut down Alec Pierce for the season
sports.summary: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.
sports.body:
Pierce has not played since aggravating a heel injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2 and the Colts’ recent roster moves have made it clear that they have shifted their attention to the 2027 season. While that may be the case, head coach Shane Steichen said on Monday that the team has not made any call about whether Pierce will return in their final six games.

“I know there’s reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season,” Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. “We have not made that determination. He’s still going through his rehab process. The only way we’ll put him out there is if he’s 100 percent. We gotta be really smart.”

Pierce has a short window to get to 100 percent before the season is over and bringing him back from a long layoff may not be the best way to ensure that he’s at full strength for next season, so it may just be a matter of when rather than if the Colts ultimately decide to shut the wideout down until next year.

sports.title: Terrion Arnold's lawyer seeks sanctions for discovery violation
sports.summary: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida.
sports.body:
On Monday, attorney Harvey Steinberg filed a motion for sanctions, arising from the alleged failure of the prosecution to timely disclose as discovery material.

The gist of the 13-page filing is that the prosecution withheld a statement from defendant Boakai Hilton until after another defendant, Arianna Del Valle, sat for a sworn, pre-trial deposition.

Hilton’s statement, per the filing, conflicts with statements made by Del Valle. By not having the Hilton statement, Steinberg was unable to properly question Del Valle about the discrepancies.

On the surface, it’s an easy fix. Steinberg should get another chance to question Del Valle under oath. At a deeper level, the situation (if it unfolded the way Steinberg alleges) speaks to the integrity of the process.

Prosecutors have immense power and discretion, which should be exercised at all times with the goal of doing justice. Sometimes, a blind desire to “win” can overcome the mandate to do justice, thereby corrupting the system.

The Hillsborough County prosecutor’s office is already dealing with an unrealted case in which “winning” may have trumped justice. A prosecutor recently resigned for failing to disclose during jury selection that the sister of a fellow prosecutor was in the jury pool for a rape trial. The woman ultimately served as the foreperson of the jury, which returned a conviction.

A new trial has been ordered, and the prosecutor who failed to disclose the relationship has resigned.

It all comes back to integrity. Are the prosecutors playing games in order get a conviction or a favorable plea deal, or are the prosecutors committed to justice in whatever form it may take?

sports.title: Report: Giants DC Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview for Maryland head coaching job
sports.summary: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.
sports.body:
Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Wilson recently had a virtual interview with the University of Maryland. Maryland fired Mike Locksley last month after a 2-5 start to the season.

Wilson grew up in Maryland and played defensive back for the Terrapins. He was a graduate assistant at the school in 2007 and 2008 before embarking on an NFL career that has also included stints with the Rams, Jets, Eagles, Ravens and Titans.

Wilson is in his first year with the Giants. They rank 12th in points allowed and seventh in yards allowed this season.

sports.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker is not in concussion protocol
sports.summary: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.
sports.body:
Canales said at his press conference that Coker is not in concussion protocol as the Panthers move toward their Week 12 game against the Buccaneers.

Coker went for a check after taking a hit from Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith during the 35-33 Panthers win. He had four catches for 47 yards during the game.

Coker has 35 catches for 440 yards and three touchdowns on the season. He is second on the team in receptions behind fellow wideout Tetairoa McMillan.

sports.title: 49ers release WR Brandon Aiyuk
sports.summary: Aiyuk will next go to waivers.
sports.body:
Two weeks after 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers have released him .

The 49ers had received a two-week roster exemption upon Aiyuk’s reinstatement. Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owed him no pay for the duration of the roster exemption.

He’ll now go to waivers, and he undoubtedly will be unclaimed. After that, he’ll become a free agent.

Many expect Aiyuk to sign with the Commanders, possibly with a practice-squad stint the first step back to the field.

Where he goes after that remains to be seen. Multiple contenders could use help at the position, if Aiyuk can perform like he did before the 2024 ACL tear that ultimately derailed his career.

sports.title: Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza: With two starts against two elite defenses, I've seen improvement
sports.summary: While Fernando Mendoza is still looking for his first win as a starting quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft displayed his considerable potential in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
sports.body:
Las Vegas was able to come back from down 17-0 to tie the game midway through the third quarter. Mendoza then engineered another touchdown drive midway through the fourth period to pull the Raiders within seven.

But the comeback effort ended when Mendoza threw a pick-six to Ja’Quan McMillian with just under two minutes left in regulation.

Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters on Monday that he saw Mendoza take steps in multiple areas.

“No. 1 is just the environment ,” Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. “That’s a very hostile environment, and I thought, overall, he did a good job of getting everybody on the same page. I thought he used his legs extremely well, extended some plays.

“For his second start in the NFL against two elite defenses, I’ve seen improvement.”

Kubiak also complimented Mendoza for the way he was able to bring the team back from being down 17.

“That’s who he is. That’s what he’s made of,” Kubiak said. “I think back to us being backed up, him taking a sack and then him making a really big third-down throw to Jack Bech. That’s what you need from your quarterback .”

Mendoza finished Sunday’s game 18-of-37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Mendoza’s next game will be his primetime debut, as the Raiders will face the Browns on Sunday night in Week 12.

sports.title: 49ers extend G.M. John Lynch's contract
sports.summary: In the offseason, the 49ers quietly extended the contract of coach Kyle Shanahan.
sports.body:
Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reports that the 49ers and G.M. John Lynch have agreed to a contract extension . Lynch, who also serves as the team’s president of football operations, was hired in early 2017. The Hall of Fame safety previously had worked for Fox.

Glazer explains that Lynch’s deal was due to expire after the 2026 season . Last night, Lynch and owner Jed York struck a handshake deal on a new contract before the Week 11 win over the Vikings.

With Shanahan and Lynch working together, the 49ers have qualified for a pair of Super Bowls. They have contended far more often than not, qualifying for the postseason in 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2025.

Before Shanahan and Lynch arrived, the 49ers hadn’t been to the playoffs since 2013.

This year, the 9-1 49ers have the inside track to the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs. They arguably have an excellent chance to win the franchise’s first Super Bowl since 1994.

sports.title: DK Metcalf: I didn't try to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye
sports.summary: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game after an altercation with the Eagles defensive back.
sports.body:
Metcalf said he “was avoiding you all” when asked why he left before players were back in the locker room after the loss and was asked what DeJean did to elicit what DeJean described as an attempt to poke him in the eye. Metcalf initially said he couldn’t remember what happened, but later denied that an eye poke was his intent.

“I didn’t try to poke him in the eye. I was just telling him. . . . I was just telling him to stop pushing me,” Metcalf said, via Joe Rutter of the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review .

The personal foul that led to Metcalf’s ejection was his second of the game and it could lead to a suspension . Metcalf called that and the notion of internal repercussions questions for others. Metcalf’s 2025 suspension for an altercation with a fan in Detroit could factor into a suspension decision and Metcalf was asked why he has struggled to remain composed at times during games.

“You have to ask the people that seemingly do that to me,” Metcalf said.

If Metcalf keeps reacting the way he did in Detroit and on Sunday, people will likely continue to try to draw a reaction that will keep him from making plays to help the Steelers so he might want to figure out a different coping mechanism whenever he is back in the lineup.

sports.title: Mike Vrabel on Drake Maye: We want to give him every opportunity to return at some point
sports.summary: Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period after suffering a fractured fibula in the Week 10 loss to the Lions.
sports.body:
But there’s still a possibility the quarterback could return to action in 2026.

With the wave of injuries the Patriots have dealt with this year, the club has not placed Maye on injured reserve — largely because the team can only have eight players return from the list.

Head coach Mike Vrabel detailed Maye’s situation during his Monday press conference as New England returns from its Week 11 bye.

“Right now, he’s not on the reserve list,” Vrabel said, via Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. “He’s not on injured reserve. He’s on the active roster. So that’s where it is today.

“I think that those things are obviously fluid, but want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time . I don’t know when that will be. I’m not sure, but I also try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week.”

While the Patriots currently have just two available quarterbacks, Vrabel said on Monday that he doesn’t anticipate the team being interested in adding Daniel Jones — or any other QB.

In 10 games this season, Maye has completed 65.6 percent of his passes for 2,330 yards with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

sports.title: Mike Vrabel says Pats don't plan to add another QB: Tommy DeVito is our starter
sports.summary: While Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period — if not the rest of the season — the Patriots are not currently inclined to add quarterback Daniel Jones.
sports.body:
That’s at least what head coach Mike Vrabel said in his Monday press conference as New England returns from its Week 11 bye.

“ Tommy’s our starter. Tommy’s our starter ,” Vrabel said, via Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, when asked directly about the possibility of adding Jones. “We’re excited about that. [He had a] good preseason. And Tommy’s improved. I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things. I think that was probably the biggest thing, just saying, ‘Hey, getting back into game action, how do you work in the pocket?’ These are things that he got so much better on when he got here.

“So, starting with those things and managing the offense and being able to get us in and out of the huddle and the right plays and just get into a flow and a tempo. And I think that some of the things that we saw in training camp, a lot of those guys that he’ll be out there throwing to some of those guys that he worked with in training camp. So, I think that there’s some carryover there.”

The Patriots currently have two quarterbacks available in DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. But at least for now, New England isn’t planning to add a third quarterback to ease the practice load.

“I think that this is also a great opportunity for Behren to improve in those reps that him and Tommy may have been splitting or Tommy taking the majority of those,” Vrabel said. “I think that that’s a great opportunity for Behren to improve in that regard of running the show team and doing those things.

“So, we will look at everything. But again, I don’t think that that’s something that’s going to happen here in the next few days.”

DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Nov. 15 loss to the Lions.

The Patriots will be on the road to face the Chargers on Sunday.

How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second […
sports.body: I think part of being a diehard NFL fan is trying to derive meaning out of everything that happens to a team, no matter how small. Think about the offseason program. How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second half of preseason games produce deep dive analysis of which players are potentially hidden gems or important depth pieces. Every now and then an OTA, training camp, or preseason, breakout turns out to be a preview of a genuine step forward by a developing player. Far more often the players and the hype are forgotten. It also goes this way in late season games when a team has fallen out of the Playoff race. Can a loss help a team secure a high Draft pick to land a franchise changing player? Can a late season surge lead to momentum carrying into a future season and be the first step in instilling a new culture? In both cases the answer is yes. Far more often, however, these games don’t have a ton of meaning either way in the long run. They amount to a bad team playing out the string. The Jets’ Week 11 victory over the Chargers has evoked passions across the fanbase. Some fans are furious about the team hurting its NFL Draft positioning. Others are happy to get the win. I don’t think there’s a “right” or a “wrong” way to be a fan. Everybody wants the same thing in the end, for the Jets to have success. Opinions simply vary on the best way to get there. I can understand fans who are hoping for as high of a pick as possible. Of course, we have seen over and over that the quality of the coaching staff and front office making the pick are generally far more important than where the pick is made. Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson were not the first quarterbacks selected in their respective Draft years. Taking it deeper, one study suggests the odds of the top player drafted at his position having a better career than the third player picked at the same position is only slightly better than a coin toss. Yes, there is the occasional case where losing helps a team land a player who legitimately changes everything, and there are cases where a meaningless late season win causes a team to miss out on that player. sports.title: Falcons waive LB Christian Harris, sign S Jammie Robinson
sports.summary: The Falcons announced a change to their roster coming out of their bye week.
sports.body:
They have waived linebacker Christian Harris. Safety Jammie Robinson was signed to the active roster off of the practice squad in a corresponding move.

Harris signed with the Falcons this offseason and appeared in seven games for Atlanta this season. Almost all of his playing time came on special teams and he was credited with four tackles.

Robinson has played in four games this season and has six tackles. He played in six games for the Falcons last season and 21 games for the Panthers over his first two seasons.

The Falcons also announced that they have signed cornerback Terell Smith to their practice squad.

sports.title: Cooper DeJean: DK Metcalf "just missed" poking me in the eye
sports.summary: Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close.
sports.body:
“ Just missed ,” DeJean said, via the Philadelphia Inquirer .

Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game after multiple incidents and two personal foul penalties, but DeJean said nothing that happened during the game could explain what had Metcalf so upset.

“We were just competing,” DeJean said. “Things like that happen in football. It wasn’t anything crazy, and no one was really saying anything. It was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me, things like that, and then it obviously carried over to whatever that was when he got thrown out.”

Metcalf had just one catch for two yards before he was kicked out, and DeJean suspects that Metcalf is mostly upset with his own production.

“He wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game,” DeJean said. “Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me.”

sports.title: Malik Nabers on sideline moment: I was just trying to watch the game
sports.summary: Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers.
sports.body:
“I vaguely remember it,” Nabers told reporters, via Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic . “But, I mean, I just remember me saying, ‘I’m good. I’m good. I wanna get back to watching the defense play.’ And that was really all, I think. Everything was going on, I was just telling the offense, ‘Let’s go, let’s go,’ I think. Jameis kind of [was] trying to calm me down, but I was fine. So I was just telling him, ‘I’m good. I’m good. I just wanna watch the game .”

The fact that Nabers navigated past Winston and got into position to watch the game seems to confirm Nabers’s explanation. He just wanted to watch the game.

The problem is that Winston’s reaction to Nabers’s initial movement created the impression that something else was happening. No quotes on the situation have emerged from Winston. It would be interesting to know why he thought Nabers needed to be restrained at a time when restraint ultimately wasn’t necessary.

Either way, the moment went viral — and more people will see that video and draw possibly inaccurate conclusions than will hear Nabers’s explanation.

Greg Rousseau turned in another multi-sack performance, and the Bi
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills added another win to their record Sunday. Once again, it was a very awkward, weird game day where Josh Allen was sacked too many times, threw a pair of interceptions, but still managed to set a brand-new NFL record. Greg Rousseau turned in another multi-sack performance, and the Bills’ defense still hasn’t given up a touchdown. Yet, somehow, another backup quarterback managed to find openings and move his offense down the field enough to make things uncomfortable. But, much like the week before when the Bills handled business against the Jets, the outcome never really felt in question. Stalled drives were more of an annoyance than a problem. Scores were more of an expectation than a celebration. And, in the end, the Bills walked off the field with a 9-1 record and woke up Monday morning as the best team in the NFL. So, with another win in the books, it’s time to hand out a few more Shout!outs. _____________________________________________________________________________ Buffalo Bills — 9-1 record It’s been 35 years since the Bills started a season this well. And, with Sunday’s win over Miami, the 2026 team has officially matched a mark that hasn’t been reached in Buffalo since the days of Jim Kelly, Thurman Thomas, and company.
