sports.body: The Buffalo Bills beat the Dolphinss 26-9 in Week 11 at Highmark Stadium, in a game that was far from perfection from Joe Brady’s but felt more impressive than last week’s win over the Jets. The Bills are now 9-1. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. Josh Allen came out ready to let it rip And I loved it. Not necessarily because Allen always made the “right” decision determining at which level to throw the football. I want defenses to be forced to think about all possible variations of Buffalo’s offense. And Allen is the best player in football. The Bills slammed their foot on the gas pedal to begin this game, and while it didn’t amount to something like three-consecutive touchdown drives — which we’ve certainly witnessed during the Allen era — it led to three pass plays of 20-plus yards and two touchdowns in the first half as Buffalo built its lead. Allen seemed adamant about dicing the Dolphins secondary through the air, and not underneath. That is Allen being Allen. Allen didn’t have a carry against the Dolphins, which now amounts to, ironically, a similar place to where we were after the Patriots loss, when the Allen criticism centered around him throwing it downfield too frequently and not running nearly enough. And what happened after that? Allen averaged 11.1 yards per attempt and ran for 121 yards on 10 carries in a 37-34 win on the road against the Rams. The safety group has become a strength Amazing, right? Even if you don’t fully agree with me, it’s impossible it ignore the difference in the play of this group recently compared to the first month or so of the season. Cole Bishop is so perfectly positioned in his box/blitz role that asks him to cover the slot underneath. He’s become a weapon as an addition to the pass rush, and his size plus explosiveness and strength allow the Bills to defend the run respectably in dime, if needed. Good early returns on Amani Hooker, as he’s allowed four catches for 47 yards with two pass breakups, nine total tackles, and a quarterback hit on three pass-rush snaps in his two contests with the Bills. And, heck, new safety No. 3, Damar Hamlin, had the biggest splash play of the group against Miami, an impressive interception at the intermediate level. Jordan Hancock played outstandingly in the safety/slot hybrid role, and the Bills even got Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin Jr. onto the field in this contest.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills RB James Cook III makes NFL history in Week 11
sports.summary: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himsel
sports.body: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himself. With Sunday’s performance, which included 89 rushing yards and a touchdown, Cook became just the second player in NFL history to rush for at least 75 yards and score a rushing touchdown in nine consecutive games, moving past three former NFL running backs who had each reached eight straight. Notably, he’s the only player in league history to put up those numbers in one season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124605029529403539?a=SI4XCAzJ3357jRKxHXM&s=20] Cook entered the game tied with Pro Football Hall of Famers John Riggins and LaDainian Tomlinson, along with George Rogers, for the second-longest streak in NFL history. Riggins accomplished the feat in 1983, Rogers did it across the 1985 and 1986 seasons, and Tomlinson matched them in 2006. The 27-year-old Cook joined that group during Buffalo’s Week 10 victory over the New York Jets. He rushed for 157 yards on 18 carries, including a career-long 74-yard touchdown run in the second half of the Bills’ 31-12 win. Now, only Terry Allen stands ahead of Cook. Allen reached 10 consecutive games with at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown while playing for Washington across the 1995 and 1996 seasons. With nine straight games behind him, Cook is now within striking distance of a record that’s stood for 30 years, but the road won’t get any easier. Kansas City and New England are next on Buffalo’s schedule, and the dates next to those names are just as challenging as the opponents. The Bills have just three days to rest, recover, and prepare to host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. If Cook is going to catch Terry Allen, he’ll have to keep his streak alive through one of the toughest stretches of Buffalo’s season.

sports.title: Mike Evans TD and Parker Washington non-TD raise more questions about NFL catch rules
sports.summary: Two big plays on Sunday renewed questions about what is and is not a catch in the NFL.
sports.body:
On Sunday afternoon, Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington caught a pass and had control with both feet down in the end zone, but it was ruled incomplete. On Sunday night, 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans didn’t have full control with both feet down as he went out of bounds in the end zone, but it was ruled a touchdown.

In the Jaguars game, former NFL referee Gene Steratore broke the play down and explained that while there was some minor movement of the football as Washington went to the ground, Washington had the ball with both feet down and never lost control.

“When Parker Washington, after the bobble, possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he’s falling,” Steratore said on the CBS broadcast. “Then I had the left foot touch. I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football. I have possession, right foot down, tap with the left foot, yes, the ball moves a little, but the right hand, in my opinion, continues to keep that secure enough, that I would say in my opinion he’s still controlling that football. I think it’s a touchdown.”

In the 49ers game, former NFL referee Terry McAulay said Evans was juggling the ball while running across the end zone and didn’t have control of it until his final step, with only one foot down in bounds.

“I don’t see him get final control until he’s got one foot down,” McAulay said. “The ball rolls around on his wrist. I don’t see it pinned to his body. When he gets control, there’s only one foot down. I think they should’ve reviewed it and reversed it to incomplete.”

Even if the NFL wants to insist that its officials got both calls right on the field, and that the replay review process was correct to uphold those calls, the league still needs to acknowledge that it has a problem on its hands if the catch rule is so confusing that even former referees who now work as on-air officiating analysts aren’t seeing what the on-field officials and the replay officials are seeing.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers calls DK Metcalf's ejection "disappointing," won't comment on message to him
sports.summary: On certain subjects, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't stop talking.
sports.body:
Regarding Sunday’s ejection of Steelers receiver DK Metcalf from the 19-16 loss to the Eagles, Rodgers said far close to nothing than something.

“ That was disappointing ,” Rodgers told reporters. “Obviously, we love DK. And I don’t know what was going on out there, what was happening. But, yeah, we can’t have two of those.”

“I’m not going to tell you that,” Rodgers said. “I’m going to talk to DK. We’re real good friends, so.”

The “I’m not going to tell you that” was unnecessary, but on brand. Rodgers flashes that aspect of his personality from time to time. And it surely will make those who have to ask him questions on a regular basis not miss him after he retires following the current season.

Besides, why is it such a secret? Rodgers already said it was “disappointing” and that “we can’t have” that. He could have just said that’s the message.

Really, what else would the message be? Metcalf needs to control his emotions. Given that Rodgers has been willing to call out others when it’s required, why should Metcalf be exempt?

Maybe that’s exactly what Metcalf needs in order to keep him from doing it again.

sports.body: In the immediate aftermath of the Buffalo Bills’ Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins, many will scratch their heads wondering what they watched unfold Sunday afternoon. To be clear her: What a strange win by the Bills. Buffalo’s offense barely resembled the group most have watched in 2026. It’s important to step back a moment, however, and realize that Buffalo has built a good, often great team. The Bills haven’t trailed in a game since October 18 against the Las Vegas Raiders (hat tip: Carson Hayek). Buffalo has also won three consecutive games by 17 or more points. What about the defense? Well, that group hasn’t allowed a touchdown in three straight games. It may be true that the Bills didn’t execute their most impressive game plan of the season, and that they strayed too far away from their true identity until crunch time. It’s clear that quarterback Josh Allen didn’t have his typically dominant effort against the Dolphins, even though he did throw for 304 yards, but he didn’t need to play lights out. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Miami Dolphins this week, winning 26-9 in what was an ugly, hard-fought game. Divisional contests are never easy, so I was instantly wary of the 16.5-point spread given Buffalo’s 8-1 record and Miami’s 1-8 record entering play. While the Bills never seemed to be in jeopardy of losing this afternoon, they definitely did not play as well as they could have. Miami’s scrappy defense fought hard, giving Buffalo’s high-powered offense trouble throughout the afternoon. At the end of the day, a win is a win whether it’s pretty or ugly, and an ugly win is far preferable to a pretty loss. There were plenty of positives to glean from today’s contest, but there were definitely some negatives, as well. Here are our horns up and horns down for Buffalo’s victory over Miami. _____________________________________________________________________________ Horns Up: Greg Rousseau In what has already been a career year, Rousseau just added to his growing stat line today. In the first half, he was an absolute menace, totaling two sacks and pressuring quarterback Kyle McCord consistently. The two sacks brought Rousseau into double-digits for the first time in his career, as he entered the day with eight. The switch to Jim Leonhard’s 3-4 front has maximized Rousseau’s ability, and he continues to shine in what is likely to be his first Pro Bowl season, and potentially his first All Pro season. Rousseau finished the game with three tackles in addition to those two sacks. Horns Up: DJ Moore Buffalo’s top wideout was the brightest spot in the passing game, especially in the first half. Moore saw seven targets in the first half, catching all of them for 79 yards and a score. Moore also had an injury scare late in the second half, as he seemed to hyperextend his knee while trying to play defense on a batted pass that was ultimately intercepted by linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. Moore was quarterback Josh Allen’s go-to guy on third downs, making plays to extend drives when Buffalo needed him most. He ultimately finished the game with 8 catches for 91 yards and a score on 10 targets. Horns Down: Josh Allen Sometimes, I really don’t know what Allen is looking at during games. sports.title: Steelers' offense is awful in loss to Eagles
sports.summary: A Philadelphia defense that previously looked like it was packing it in on the season stepped up in a big way today.
sports.body:
But as Chris Berman used to say to the late, great Tom Jackson on NFL Primetime , That’s why they play the games.

It was the Eagles who came out looking like a team in contention, and the Steelers who came out flat in a 19-16 Eagles win in Philadelphia.

The Steelers’ offense was awful, particularly running the ball. Aaron Rodgers was the leading rusher with 29 yards on five carries. Jaylen Warren, who has played so well for most of this season, managed just 28 yards on nine carries, and Rico Dowdle had 15 yards on five carries.

Pittsburgh didn’t score a touchdown until 1:21 remained in the fourth quarter, Aaron Rodgers hit Max Hurleman in the end zone for 20 yards.

Steelers receiver DK Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls, the second of which was called as taunting but appeared to involve Metcalf trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. Metcalf finished the game with one catch for two yards and had the worst of his many bad games this season.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made four field goals, including a 53-yarder in the third quarter and a 55-yarder in the fourth quarter that kept Philly on top even as its offense stagnated.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton wasn’t great, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards, but he showed a little bit of promise with both his arm and his legs, and played well enough that there’s no reason the Eagles shouldn’t stick with him and see what he can do. Saquon Barkley also wasn’t great, but he did manage a 38-yard touchdown run.

The Steelers, who still haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965, fall to 6-4 on the season. The Eagles improve to 3-7.

sports.title: Travis Kelce moves past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in TD catches by a tight end
sports.summary: For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone.
sports.body:
And Kelce has also secured another milestone in his storied career.

Kelce capped the Chiefs’ first drive with an 8-yard touchdown catch, giving Kansas City an early 7-0 lead over Arizona.

The score also moved Kelce past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in touchdowns by a tight end. Only Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez are ahead of Kelce on the list.

The possession lasted 11 plays and went 72 yards to the end zone, taking 5:14 off the clock.

Patrick Mahomes was 4-of-5 on the drive for 36 yards, converting a pair of third downs. He hit Rashee Rice for a 15-yard gain on one third down and the touchdown to Kelce was the second.

Rookie Emmett Johnson is once again off to a strong start, taking six carries for 36 yards while also catching a screen for an 8-yard gain.

sports.body: In Week 10, Cade Klubnik got his first NFL regular season action in relief of an injured Smith. Klubnik played most of the Jets’ second half loss to the Buffalo Bills. In Week 11, it appears Smith will regain his starting role. We asked fans in our SB Nation Reacts survey whether this is the right call. A narrow majority said Klubnik should start this game. [Image: https://platform.ganggreennation.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/86/2026/11/Jets_2_111626.png?quality=90&strip=all] That is about as close of a result as you can get. It should be noted, however, that we asked a similar question a week ago, and only 28 percent of Jets fans voted that Klubnik should start. It seems like merely seeing Klubnik on the field was enough to sway a large number of fans because his play against Buffalo certainly wasn’t spectacular. Overall Jets fan confidence is down after the loss to the Bills. Only 20 percent of voters say they are confident in the team’s direction down from 28 percent last week. [Image: https://platform.ganggreennation.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/86/2026/11/Jets_1_111626.png?quality=90&strip=all] I’m not sure much a win over the Chargers will improve confidence, but I could see the number falling into single digits with a loss along with the proportion of fans who want to see Klubnik rising quite a bit. sports.body: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. Today, for the first time in three weeks, we’re not handing out a pre-blame ball. They allowed just 15 rushing yards last week against the Baltimore Ravens.
